title: Seven Years After a Stage 3 Diagnosis, a Laredo Couple Urges Screenings and Hope
excerpt: Ruben Vela was diagnosed with Stage 3 pancreatic cancer in 2019. Seven years later he is back at work, running and cycling — and he and his wife Patty are urging Laredoans to get checked.
content:
Seven years ago, Ruben Vela of Laredo was told he had Stage 3 pancreatic cancer. Today he is back at work, running and cycling — and he and his wife Patty are using their story to urge others to pay attention to their health.

Ruben was diagnosed in 2019, at age 62, according to the Laredo Morning Times. His symptoms had started the year before — bloating and back pain that were first attributed to acid reflux or a gallbladder problem. A scan eventually found a 3.7-centimeter tumor on the head of his pancreas.

He underwent a Whipple procedure in January 2019 at Methodist Hospital in San Antonio. Surgeons removed 18 lymph nodes, 10 of them cancerous. He then had chemotherapy and 25 radiation treatments, and has continued follow-up care in Laredo with oncologist Dr. Frank Enriquez. His surgeon was Dr. Michael O’Leary.

Patty credits faith, family support and Dr. O’Leary’s encouragement for Ruben’s recovery, and she urges people to keep up with annual checkups and to take persistent symptoms seriously.

The couple’s story comes during Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month. November 20 is World Pancreatic Cancer Day. Figures cited from the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network put the 2025 U.S. toll at about 67,440 people diagnosed and about 51,980 deaths, with a five-year survival rate of 13 percent.

The Velas, married 35 years, also remember Ruben’s sister Joanne Vela, who died in 2010 at age 52 from breast cancer.
